title: T.O. police cleared in man's shooting
article: The civilian agency that investigates police shootings has concluded that Toronto officers were justified in the fatal daylight shooting of a man in a mid-town park in June.
O'brien Christopher-Reid was shot as police attempted to arrest him at Edwards Gardens after they received calls that a man was carrying a knife.

Deadly force in Christopher-Reid's June 13 shooting was warranted "because he refused to comply with the officers' demands that he drop his weapon and, indeed, advanced on the officers uttering threats," Special Investigations Unit director James Cornish said Thursday in a release.

Officers used pepper spray on Christopher-Reid, 26, to no effect, the SIU said. He ran and was pursued by the three officers, who drew their firearms when Christopher-Reid pulled a knife from his pants and held it over his head.
